fields.what_it_is: Reline Small Stature is a small stature fixation system for pediatric spinal care, designed as a premium solution for pediatric deformity patients. It leverages innovation, simple and elegant design, and clinical experience. The system includes pedicle screws that accept 4.5 or 5.0mm rods in titanium (Ti6Al4V) or cobalt chrome (CoCr), featuring a low-profile tulip design with Helical Flange Locking Technology to reduce head splay and minimize cross-threading. Screw shanks feature a double lead thread for efficient screw insertion and are available in a solid design. Screw shanks and load rings are color-coded to the shank diameter. The portfolio includes polyaxial, polyaxial reduction, monoaxial, uniplanar, open, and iliac screw types. Lock screws come in open and closed types, compatible with 4.5 and 5.0mm rods. Rods are available in 4.5mm and 5.0mm diameters in titanium or cobalt chrome, with titanium rods color-coded by diameter and featuring solid lines for sagittal orientation, and cobalt chrome rods featuring a textured surface and dashed lines. Rod-to-rod connectors include open-open, open-closed, and closed-closed types, and traditional growing rod (TGR) connectors in 50mm, 70mm, and 90mm sizes. Cross connectors are low-profile, fixed or adjustable, with sizes from 11mm to 60mm, compatible with 4.5mm and 5.0mm rods. Hooks come in various anatomically designed blades with throat diameters from 4.0mm to 10.0mm. The system is manufactured from Ti-6Al-4V ELI per ASTM F136 and ISO 5832-3, Grade 4 CP Ti per ASTM F67, or cobalt chromium per ASTM F1537.
fields.sizing_specs:
**Pedicle Screw Portfolio**
- Accepts 4.5 or 5.0mm rods in titanium (Ti6Al4V) or cobalt chrome (CoCr).
- Low-profile tulip design with Helical Flange Locking Technology.
- Screw shanks feature double lead thread, available in solid design.
- Screw shanks and load rings color-coded to shank diameter:
  | Shank/load ring colors | Screw diameters |
  |------------------------|-----------------|
  | Bronze                 | 4.0mm           |
  | Green                  | 4.5mm           |
  | Light blue             | 5.0mm           |
  | Gold                   | 5.5mm           |
  | Magenta                | 6.5mm           |
  | Dark blue              | 7.5mm           |
  | Purple                 | 8.5mm           |
- Screw types: Polyaxial, Polyaxial Reduction, Monoaxial, Uniplanar, Open, Iliac.

**Lock Screws**
- Open lock screw: for open tulips, compatible with 4.5 and 5.0mm rods.
- Closed lock screw: for closed Iliac Offset Connectors and closed Rod to Rod connectors, compatible with 4.5 and 5.0mm rods.

**Rods**
- Diameters: 4.5mm and 5.0mm.
- Materials: Titanium (Ti6Al4V) or cobalt chrome (CoCr).
- Titanium rods: Color-coded by diameter, feature solid lines for sagittal orientation.
- Cobalt chrome rods: Textured surface, marked with dashed line for sagittal orientation.
- 4.5mm rods: Spline end.
- 5.0mm rods: Hex end.

**Rod-to-rod Connectors**
- Types: Open-Open, Open-Closed, Closed-Closed.
- Compatibility: 4.5/5.0mm–4.5/5.0mm, 4.5/5.0mm–5.0/6.0mm.
- Traditional Growing Rod (TGR) Connectors: 50mm, 70mm, 90mm.

**Cross Connectors**
- Low-profile, fixed or adjustable.
- Fixed sizes: 11mm, 13mm, and 15-30mm in increments of 2.5mm.
- Adjustable sizes: ranges span from 22mm up to 60mm.
- Rod compatibility: 4.5mm, 5.0mm.
- Color-coded: 4.5mm (gold), 5.0mm (magenta).

**Hooks**
- Throat diameters: 4.0mm, 6.0mm, 8.0mm, 10.0mm (color-coded).
- Types: Standard hooks (Lamina narrow, Lamina wide, Pedicle, Transverse process, Offset left, Offset right), Alternative hooks (Hyperfit, Sidewinder left, Sidewinder right).
fields.indications: When used as a pedicle screw fixation system, the NuVasive Reline System is intended to provide immobilization and stabilization of spinal segments in skeletally mature patients as an adjunct to fusion in the treatment of the following acute and chronic instabilities or deformities of the posterior thoracic, lumbar, and sacral spine: 1. Degenerative disc disease (as defined by back pain of discogenic origin with degeneration of the disc confirmed by patient history and radiographic studies) 2. Degenerative spondylolisthesis with objective evidence of neurologic impairment 3. Fracture 4. Dislocation 5. Scoliosis 6. Kyphosis 7. Spinal tumor and/or 8. Failed previous fusion (pseudoarthrosis). When used for posterior non-cervical screw fixation in pediatric patients, NuVasive Reline System is indicated as an adjunct to fusion to treat adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. Additionally the NuVasive Reline System is intended to treat pediatric patients diagnosed with the following conditions: spondylolisthesis / spondylolysis, and fracture caused by tumor and/or trauma. Pediatric pedicle screw fixation is limited to a posterior approach and is intended to be used with autograft and/or allograft. The NuVasive Reline System is also indicated for the treatment of severe spondylolisthesis (Grades 3 and 4) of the L5-S1 vertebral joint in skeletally mature patients receiving fusion by autogenous bone graft, having the device fixed or attached to the lumbar and sacral spine (L3 to sacrum), with removal of the implants after attainment of a solid fusion. When used as an anterolateral non-pedicle screw system in the thoracic and lumbar spine, the NuVasive Reline System is also intended for the following indications: 1. Degenerative disc disease (as defined by back pain of discogenic origin with degeneration of the disc confirmed by patient history and radiographic studies), 2. Spinal stenosis, 3. Spondylolisthesis, 4. Spinal deformities, 5. Fracture, 6. Pseudoarthrosis, 7. Tumor resection, and/or 8. Failed previous fusion.
fields.contraindications: Contraindications include but are not limited to: 1. Infection, local to the operative site. 2. Signs of local inflammation. 3. Patients with known sensitivity to the materials implanted. 4. Patients who are unwilling to restrict activities or follow medical advice. 5. Patients with inadequate bone stock or quality. 6. Patients with physical or medical conditions that would prohibit beneficial surgical outcome. 7. Reusable or multiple uses.
fields.compatible_with: In order to achieve additional levels of fixation, the Reline System rods may be connected to the Armada System. Do not use Reline System with components of other systems than Armada System.
fields.use_notes:
Pedicle Preparation: Locate entry point, perforate cortex with burr, create pilot hole with Gearshift Probe, inspect with Dual-ended Ball Tip Pedicle Probe, self-tapping screws may be inserted or tap if preferred using Fixed or Ratcheting Handle with appropriately sized Tap, inspect again before screw insertion. NVM5 monitors pedicle integrity during preparation.

Screw Insertion: Select screw type and matching screwdriver, attach fixed or ratcheting handle, load screwdriver into screw shank, introduce into pilot hole and advance to desired depth, release screwdriver, ensure tulip motion for polyaxial screws, use Screw Adjuster for depth adjustment or Head Adjuster for tulip orientation, test screws with NVM5 Stimulation Probe.

Rod Contouring: Measure construct length, bend rod using French Bender (small, medium, large radii) or Plate Bender for tight/large radii bends, use longitudinal lines for sagittal alignment.

Rod and Lock Screw Insertion: Place rod into implants using Rod Holder, confirm sagittal alignment with lines, use Lock Screw Starter to load and deliver lock screw, adjust tulip with Joystick Head Adjuster if needed, use Rod Holders for complex manipulation or rotation (attach with ratchet release trigger, compress handle to fix, rotate in steps with two holders, tighten lock screws after rotation), rod rotation also possible with Rod Rotation Wrench on hex or spline ends.

Rod Reduction with Saber Reducer: For up to 40mm reduction, retract threaded sleeve, capture rod in slot, align to tulip, engage tulip with downward pressure (audible/tactile feedback), place Reduction Handle on sleeve and turn clockwise until black line overlaps reducer end, use Reduction Bell Attachment for multiple levels, insert lock screw with Lock Screw Starter after reduction, remove reducer by depressing buttons and pulling up, ease removal by turning handle ¼ counterclockwise before lock screw delivery.

In Situ Rod Bending: Use Sagittal Bender (angled and straight tips) for lordosis/kyphosis by compressing toward or away, use Coronal Bender (tips in 4.5mm gold or 5.0mm silver) for coronal correction by compressing arms toward each other, use Coronal Bender Extension Link for multiple levels.

Compression and Distraction: Provisionally tighten one lock screw, leave adjacent loose, use Parallel or Hinged Compressor/Distractor over rod against tulip heads, deliver compression/distraction, provisionally tighten loose screw before final tightening, do not final tighten under force.

Final Tightening: Tighten all lock screws to 70 in-lbs torque using Torque Handle attached to Final Lock Screw Driver with Counter-torque over tulip.

Cross Connectors: Measure distance between rods with Cross Connector Measurement Guide. For low-profile adjustable: prepare Cross Connector Holder by rotating top counter-clockwise, place over connector end and rotate clockwise to engage, place ends flush on rod, attach Cross Connector 30 in-lb Torque Handle to Cross Connector Driver, insert into Holder, verify cam locked (wide arc counter-clockwise), final tighten center lock nut with Adjustable Cross-Connector Counter-torque. For fixed: use Fixed Cross Connector Benders for fine adjustments by placing connector in slot and sliding thumb piece to attach, compress benders for desired bend, then follow same Holder and driver steps as adjustable.

Growing Rod Constructs: For traditional growing rod (TGR) construct, cut long rod into two shorter lengths, insert into TGR Connector with 5mm clearance between rods, bend rod to curvature, adjust rod lengths in connector, final tighten connector lock screws, insert rod subfascially from proximal to distal opening, rotate rod into sagittal plane with rod gripper, provisionally lock proximal and distal rods, use Saber and Reduction Handle for rod persuasion if needed, apply distraction if necessary, final tighten lock screws with Torque T-handle, Final Driver, and Counter-torque, use autograft for fusion, take final fluoroscopy. For distraction: expose TGR Connector, loosen one lock screw, place TGR Distractor tips into slot between rods, compress handles to distract, final tighten lock screw.

Reduction Screws: Insert following Pedicle Preparation and Screw Insertion steps, use Polyaxial Reduction Driver, slide Reduction Screw Counter-torque over screw head until flush on rod, reduce rod by threading lock screw down extended tulip with Lock Screw Starter while applying downward force on Counter-torque, rod fully reduced when lock screw sits below recessed ridge at base of extended tulip, final tighten lock screws before breaking off extensions, use Reduction Screw Break-off Tool over extended tulip with thumb piece inward, rock medial/lateral to break free, expel extensions by sliding thumb piece distally, use Reduction Screw Cap as alternative to Counter-torque to restrict tulip splay.

Hooks: Prepare hook site with Pedicle Elevator, Lamina Elevator, or Transverse Process Elevator, choose inserter (Threaded Hook Inserter, Bilateral Hook Inserter, Unilateral Hook Inserter), for impaction partially thread Threaded Hook Inserter into hook, insert Hook Pusher into rod slot under inserter and tighten until secure.

Iliac Screws: Expose posterior superior iliac spine, decorticate entry point with burr or rongeur, create pilot hole with Iliac Gearshift Probe aiming above greater sciatic notch, inspect with Dual-ended Ball Tip Pedicle Probe, tap pilot hole, re-inspect, select iliac screw and insert with Polyaxial Screwdriver, advance to desired depth, use Screw Adjuster for depth adjustment. For Offset Iliac Connectors: determine offset length, use Rod Holder to insert connector shaft into iliac screw rod slot, use Unilateral Inserter for open offset connectors, insert lock screw with Lock Screw Starter and provisionally tighten, final tighten with Open Offset Connector Counter-torque.

Vertebral Body Derotation: Use preoperative radiographs to identify apex for en bloc or caudal-neutral vertebral body for segmental derotation. Segmental: align Saber Reducers with tulips on neutral and first superior rotated vertebral bodies, apply downward pressure to engage, connect Coupled Segmental Derotation Link to derotation towers across each body and lock set screws, provisionally tighten lock screws on neutral body and leave loose on rotated bodies, derotate rotated body into neutral position using neutral as reference, provisionally tighten lock screws with Long Lock Screw Driver to hold correction, repeat for next levels. En bloc: align Saber Reducers with tulips on selected vertebral bodies, apply downward pressure to engage, connect Coupled Segmental Derotation Link to towers across each body and lock set screws, connect all links with Derotation Clamp and squeeze to engage adjacent towers, rotate black locking lever to locked position, construct segmental frame inferior or superior as reference, provisionally lock at least one lock screw at neutral segment above and below Derotation Towers, rotate en bloc construct around rod until vertebral bodies neutral, provisionally tighten lock screws with Ratcheting Handle and Long Lock Screw Driver, assistant can push on rib hump during derotation.

Implant Removal: Cross Connector: attach Cross Connector 30 in-lb Torque T-handle to Cross Connector Driver (T20), for adjustable first loosen center lock screw counterclockwise, loosen connection to rod by inserting driver into cam above each rod and rotating counterclockwise 180°, grasp with Cross Connector Holder and lift to remove. Lock Screw: seat Open Screw Counter-torque over tulip, with Ratcheting T-handle attached to Lock Screw Driver insert through Counter-torque into lock screw and turn counterclockwise to loosen, repeat for rod-rod connectors. Rod and/or Rod-to-Rod Connector: after lock screw removal, grasp rod with Rod Holder and lift to remove. Screw: insert appropriate screwdriver (C-Star25 or T25) into screw head and secure by turning silver knob clockwise, remove by rotating counterclockwise, use Screw Adjuster for removal if preferred, for provisional locking screw use Fixed Screwdriver and rotate counterclockwise in orbital motion. Hook: grasp with Implant Holder and slide cephalad or caudal to remove.

General: Use NVM5 System for neuromonitoring, place patient prone, ensure fluoroscopic access, use Core Trays (RSSCOREIMP, RSSCOREIN1, RSSCOREIN2, RSSURODCUTIN) and Ancillary Trays as needed, refer to Instructions for Use for complete list of intended uses, device description, contraindications, warnings, and precautions. Pivoting rod-rod connectors must be used in pairs. Ø4.75 mm rods are not for main rod construct in pedicle screw tulip but for supporting rod in multiple rod technique. Safety and effectiveness not established for growing rod construct; device only for definitive fusion at all instrumented levels. Correct implant selection is important. Do not implant in patients with known sensitivity to materials. Do not use with bone cement or in patients with poor bone quality. Use only with saline or radiopaque dye. Ensure all components ideally fixated before closure. Patient should limit postoperative activity. Single use only; do not reuse. MR safety unknown; scanning may result in injury. Do not combine with other systems except Armada. Use only designated instruments. Iliac screws have single lead thread and must be used with single lead taps. Be careful with break point as Tulip may be sharp. Silencer and Gator Reducers not compatible with Reduction Screws or Reduction Uni-planar Screws; only Matador Reducer and Rocker may be used. Remove K-wire when screw reaches posterior wall of pedicle to avoid kink. Ensure K-wire not advancing during preparation; use lateral fluoroscopy. Final-tighten all lock screws with Counter-torque and Torque T-handle; do not final-tighten through compression instruments. Do not over compress or distract to avoid screw loosening or pullout. Bulleted nose and faceted portion of rod must extend outside most inferior or superior tulip; set screw cannot be locked on this portion. Cross connectors are rod diameter specific and cannot be used on tapered sections of tapered rods; attach only on constant diameter sections.
fields.also_known_as: Reline Small Stature, NuVasive Reline System
